rationale: The workflow is an autotools/C CI that installs system dependencies via apt-get in every job and builds/tests with make; it has no Python/pip/pyproject.toml dependency-install step. The only directly measured caching evidence in the retrieved records (P-LIT-DISTRIBUTED-CACHE experiments) adds an actions/cache entry for ~/.cache/pip keyed on hashFiles('pyproject.toml') in a Python pytest workflow, which has no equivalent here. The general P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache pattern requires a lockfile/environment cache input and lists mutable cached content as a contraindication; apt has no lockfile and apt-get update refreshes package lists each run, so a safe cache key/invalidation cannot be established from the provided evidence. Other patterns (matrix fail-fast, custom timeout, cancel-stale) either already match intended coverage, lack representative duration history for a safe timeout, or would alter required-check semantics without verified required-check status. No supported, prerequisite-meeting optimization applies, so the workflow is preserved unchanged.
